html:
The Libyan civil war of 2011 began with protests in Benghazi in February 2011, part of the Arab Spring, and ended in October with the death of Muammar Gaddafi.

Gaddafi's forces fired on protesters, and the east rose in revolt. As his army closed on Benghazi in March, the UN Security Council authorised force to protect civilians, and NATO began air strikes. The rebels took Tripoli in August. Gaddafi was caught and killed near his home town of Sirte on 20 October.

The war ended one-man rule but left a land of armed militias and no army or institutions. Within three years Libya split again in the second civil war.
sum: The Libyan civil war of 2011 began with protests in Benghazi in February 2011, part of the Arab Spring, and ended in October with the death of Muammar Gaddafi.
